prediction.likelyOutcome: Given conceded liability, severe physical encumbrance of improved parcels, and the government's failure to offer any competing valuation, the Kotis Entities are very likely to recover a substantial just compensation award — the government's zero/nominal theories are weak on this record. The principal uncertainty is quantum: the court may meaningfully discount Dr. Kilpatrick's $44.74 million figure based on credited methodology criticisms (national cap rate survey, comparable selection) even without a rival number to anchor a specific reduction, plus interest from the October 11, 2019 taking date.

outcome.description: After the valuation trial the Court of Federal Claims adopted Dr. Kilpatrick's before-and-after values for all thirteen parcels but struck his privacy-wall component, awarding just compensation of $42,641,740 (before values $66,179,431, after values $23,537,691) plus interest at the Moody's Aaa corporate bond rate compounded annually, against a demand of $44,744,774; it also denied the government's motion to reopen the record. No attorneys' fees were addressed in this opinion. This is the trial-level decision; no appellate ruling is reflected.
